For users considering switching from Windows to Mac, software restrictions are virtually nonexistent. The Mac platform can not only run all major PC applications, but also offers countless practical applications that are exclusive to Mac.

The only major exception is gaming. However, the latest tests show that whether through official or unofficial means, Windows games now run better on Mac than ever before...

Apple provides a dedicated game porting toolkit to help developers evaluate the performance of their Windows games on Mac, with the aim of encouraging and facilitating the porting of games to the Mac platform.

However, according to Macworld's Filipe Esposito, this toolkit has also been used by gamers to unofficially run Windows software on Mac. He himself is one such user, and notes that the latest test version has brought significant performance improvements, citing Grand Theft Auto V as an example.

I spent a few days testing the game porting toolkit 4 beta on a MacBook Pro equipped with an M4 Pro chip, and found that the performance improvements fundamentally change the experience of running demanding Windows games...Using the same M4 Pro MacBook Pro with 24GB of memory, the same game settings, and the same benchmark, the frame rate of GTA V jumped from about 106 fps on GPTK 3 to about 176 fps on GPTK 4 beta, an increase of roughly 66%. The game ran smoothly at medium-to-high quality settings in 2K resolution.

He acknowledges that not every game will achieve such remarkable results, but he hopes these advances will encourage game studios to consider Mac as a viable platform.
